output.summary: Attrition (14.1%; seniors 13.6%) is below the firm's 5-year average and the regional peer median (18%), so there is no retention crisis. Both September resignations were decided months earlier for unrelated reasons (in-house move, spouse's residency) and the leavers said the Friday change was not a factor. The Friday change deliberately traded flexibility for junior supervision and lowered flexibility satisfaction (3.9 to 3.1). Intent to stay is flat, and the low-flexibility group's intent matches the rest. Junior training satisfaction rose, but the gain is confounded by the new curriculum, and skill-gap closure is unmeasured. Recommend reporting the facts, keeping the existing monitoring triggers and January review, and communicating the rationale. A bonus or reversal is premature, and identifying the associates who complained would be harmful.
